general_oracle_interface_compatibility.assessment: Current general classical and quantum Definitions fix the procedure at encoded length and declared public data; hidden encoding is not readable input. Simon local public data are address width n and output width m (plus the recovery tolerance). The general encoded-length variable is not Simon address width: one may index fixed-(n,m) oracles by their lexicographic m*2^n-bit tables at a common encoded length, without revealing them. a(length)=n and b(length)=m on that fixed family; different widths can be handled as separate declared families/public parameters. At n=1,m=0 the sole empty table labels the only constant oracle. All Simon gates, initial states, instruments, pivot operations and final outputs depend only on public data and observed outcomes. The classical posterior proof fixes these public widths and random tape across hidden masks/labels. Standard XOR access and empty target width agree. No f-dependent preparation, final predicate or readable code is required; no extra controlled/inverse query is used. No general-interface repair is needed.
